# M11-NOV-01a3b3: result-conditioned search comparison design

**Decision, 2026-09-25.** The frozen eligibility gate requires three source-backed positive/control pairs whose *initial* maintained-validator results contain independent, central-mechanism-supporting prior art. The first six-pair bank qualified only GPX4. The second bank stopped on its registered first error after three complete pairs and qualified none of those three. Its remaining calls cannot be replayed as the same preregistered screen after the parser correction. No accepted triplet exists, so a confirmatory comparison or adoption claim is unavailable.

This is an **external technique** inspired by [Sakana's repeated novelty search](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/generate_ideas.py#L285-L492), not a Google-backed requirement. The current local validation path searches once per draft through [`validate_search.py`](../../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/generation/literature_tools/validate_search.py), parses papers, and gives them to the existing per-paper analysis. The question is whether one bounded result-conditioned follow-up can recover source-backed prior art without conflating distinct ideas; it is not whether a model can declare an idea novel.

## Alternatives and choice

1. Resume the stopped second screen after the fix: rejected. Its registered stop-on-first-error rule makes that a new experiment, and the first three completed positives did not meet the unchanged central-support criterion.
2. Screen another hand-picked bank immediately: deferred. Two source banks have yielded only one qualifying pair. Further case search before testing a concrete candidate risks spending more effort selecting for a favorable baseline.
3. **Chosen:** run one *exploratory*, prospective paired pilot over **all six** pairs from the already frozen first bank, in its original order, with no eligibility selection or draft editing. These are exposed development cases, not a new holdout. Their primary-paper target and distinct-control anchor IDs were frozen before this exact prompt/runner adaptation and before the pilot's outcomes, so exact-ID retrieval differences are observable even when an initial result is merely related or off topic. The pilot can decide whether the one frozen adaptation merits confirmatory work; it cannot establish general scientific quality or authorize release by itself.

The fixed cases come from [`novelty-fixture-bank-prereg-v1.json`](novelty-fixture-bank-prereg-v1.json):

## Boundary to freeze before calls

Build and verify the runner offline first, then commit a complete preregistration with its code/config hashes, exact static and conditioned prompts, selected qualified zero-price model and served-model rule, request options, input hashes, cache isolation, result schema, and stop conditions. No target or anchor PMID may enter either model prompt, PubMed query, tool parameter, or blinded relevance packet; reject a generated query containing one before sending it. The target IDs are revealed only to the scorer after result capture. The project model route must pass a fresh official exact-zero price/admission check before live calls, set the request-level zero-price cap and one-attempt boundary, and record the model actually served. A changed or unqualified route stops the batch; baseline/candidate comparisons must use the same actually served model.

For each of the 12 frozen drafts, issue the first search through the actual configured validation tool with the current `draft[:200]` query and at most three papers. Give **identical first-search evidence** to both arms. The static arm generates one follow-up query from the draft alone; it must be generated before its caller receives the first-search results. The candidate arm generates one follow-up query from the same draft plus the first result titles and available abstracts; paper IDs remain in the private scorer/provenance record and never enter either model prompt. Each arm gets one model call and one further call through the same PubMed tool, with at most three papers. Both follow-ups use the same selected model, request budget, tool parameters and evaluation date window. The two arms differ only in visibility of the first-search evidence. The maximum is **36 outer MCP tool calls** (12 shared first searches and 24 follow-ups) and **24 zero-price model calls**, without retries or auxiliary models. This is not a 36-request NCBI HTTP cap: each tool call may run up to three ESearch relaxation rungs, then fetch metadata for up to nine candidate IDs and issue PMC-link requests. The runner must preserve the internal rung/ID/request trace and stay within the maintained tool's existing bounds. Unique slugs and a fresh cache prevent result carry-over. A first retrieval, model, rate-limit, billing-admission or parser error stops the whole pilot and leaves it inconclusive; no paid substitution or silent fallback is allowed.

**Primary metric:** exact positive target-PMID recall in the union of the two three-paper results, candidate versus matched static follow-up, scored over all six positives. The candidate must gain at least one target while losing none found by the static arm. **Non-regression:** no loss of any distinct-control own-anchor hit, no increase in cross-pair positive-target hits in controls, no increase in blinded unrelated-paper fraction, and complete per-paper query/rung/PMID/source provenance. A blinded reviewer labels full-draft central support, related-only or unrelated on public abstracts without arm, rank or target identity; an LLM judgment supplements rather than replaces observable IDs. Retrieval errors and incomplete outcomes are reported separately, never scored as novelty or as no-hit successes.

If the frozen candidate fails the primary or a non-regression criterion on the completed six-pair pilot, reject **that adaptation** as unsupported in this campaign; do not infer that every possible iterative-search technique fails. If it passes, retain the mechanism as promising and require a newly preregistered, independently eligible three-pair comparison before implementation/release; the exposed pilot alone cannot satisfy the campaign's scientific-quality acceptance rule. If a clean pilot cannot complete under zero-cost/rate-limit conditions, keep the candidate inconclusive and open. No result-conditioned query has been run for this design decision.
